title: Cost-surge routing: graceful fallbacks and GPU-priority policy
creator: Tomás Rivera
description: Problem: Customers observe intermittent cost spikes when spot capacity is scarce or on-demand price surges in a region. Current routing defaults either over-prefer spot (leading to higher eviction/latency) or fall back to naive on-demand selections without considering model variant cost profiles or quantization compatibilities. We need an operator-friendly routing policy that: 1) enforces per-customer and per-route budget caps, 2) biases selection across regions and tiers to balance latency and unit cost, 3) prioritizes GPU types based on model memory/compute/quant profile, and 4) performs graceful fallback to lower-cost model variants or different quantization paths when budget thresholds or eviction risk is reached.
proposal: Introduce a two-layer policy: A budget guard + probabilistic preference layer. Budget guard tracks sliding-window spend per route and per-customer; once soft-cap breached, it reduces preference for expensive options by a configurable decrement. The probabilistic preference layer assigns weights to candidates (region x tier x GPU-class x model-variant) derived from a composite score: Score = w_latency*latency_norm + w_cost*cost_norm + w_reliability*(1-eviction_prob). We normalize by tenant SLAs and allow policy overrides per customer. GPU selection rules embed quantization compatibility (e.g., int8-compatible models prefer T4/Inferentia-like classes; large-context models prefer A100-style classes). Fallback chain: primary variant -> quantized variant (lower VRAM) -> smaller-architecture variant -> cross-region on-demand. Each step annotates expected quality delta and cost delta.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Routing engine exposes per-route soft/hard budget caps and enforces soft-cap throttles within <5% tokens of expected reduction. 2) In canary traffic, preference weights reduce selection of expensive region/tiers by at least configured decrement when soft-cap is hit. 3) When eviction_prob>threshold, requests are routed to a fallback variant within 200ms additional scheduling time for 95% of cases. 4) Integration tests that simulate spot-eviction and on-demand price spike demonstrate no SLA breach for prioritized tenants and a measurable unit-cost reduction for best-effort tenants. 5) Dashboard surfaces per-customer spend, current cap state, and fallback counts.
design_decisions: - Use sliding-window (1h, 24h) spend metrics rather than instantaneous token counters to avoid oscillation. - Soft caps trigger probabilistic degradation (0..1) rather than absolute blocking to preserve throughput. - Keep default weight set conservative (w_latency=0.6, w_cost=0.3, w_reliability=0.1) but make tunable per-customer. - Quantization-aware GPU ranking: maintain per-model metadata (expected peak_vram, op_friendly_kernels) in catalog and match to GPU capability tags. - Rollout path: feature-flagged canary -> tenant opt-in -> global opt-in.
implementation_notes: Backend: routing-core changes to accept candidate metadata (estimated_cost_per_token, eviction_prob, gpu_class, variant_quality_score). Budget service: extend usage-store to calculate rolling spend and expose gRPC endpoints with fast checks for route decisions. Policy engine: evaluate composite score and sample against probabilistic throttle. Runtime: annotate selected node with 'fallback_origin' and 'budget_reason' for tracing. Metrics: emit 'fallback_taken', 'budget_softcap_active', 'candidate_score' tags. Config: per-tenant YAML policy with overrides and emergency hard-cap.
tradeoffs: - Complexity vs predictability: probabilistic throttles are smoother but harder to reason about; chose them to avoid sudden capacity cliffs. - Quality vs cost: aggressive fallback to smaller variants reduces spend but may increase hallucination risk; we provide per-customer override and an explicit quality SLA flag. - Latency cost: cross-region fallback increases latency; we limit cross-region fallback to best-effort routes only.
test_plan: - Unit tests for score calculation and budget decrement math. - Integration test harness simulating spot eviction events and price spikes using synthetic region signals. - Canary: route 5% of traffic for 2 tenants with differing SLAs and verify fallback counts and spend changes over 24h. - Load test: ensure routing decision path adds <3ms median overhead and <25ms p95 overhead. - Chaos test: force frequent spot evictions and validate graceful degradation and tracing continuity.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'cost_surge_fallback_v1'. 2) Deploy routing-core + budget-service to staging. 3) Internal canary on non-critical tenants (1%) for 48h. 4) Tenant opt-in (customer success) 5) Ramp to 10% and measure. 6) Full enable for best-effort tier with monitoring and quick rollback path.
metrics_and_dashboards: Primary metrics: per-tenant spend_{1h,24h}, fallback_count_by_variant, candidate_selection_distribution, eviction_prob_histogram, avg_token_cost. Dashboards: - Cost Surge Summary (per-region, per-tier) - Per-Tenant Budget Status - Fallbacks by model variant - Latency impact of cross-region fallbacks. Links: https://console.internal.redwood/dashboards/cost-surge-summary, https://console.internal.redwood/dashboards/tenant-budget-status
